pageCache.pageTitle: Edward Wilson Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
A key member of Captain Scott’s Antarctic Expedition Team, Edward Wilson was an explorer, artist, doctor and natural scientist. He lost his life alongside his team in 1912. Inscribed on his memorial is the final verse of Tennyson’s poem, Ulysses:
“Strong in will to strive, to seek, to find and not to yield.”
At Edward Wilson Primary School, we are inspired, challenged and motivated by Edward Wilson; thus, our motto is: ‘To seek, to find and not to yield’. We hold the highest aspirations and expectations for our pupils, and by extension, our staff, families, governors and supporters.
Here at Edward Wilson, we nurture curiosity in learning in a fun atmosphere encouraging all our school community to achieve the best they can. Inspired by the life of Antarctic explorer Edward Wilson, perseverance and ambition underpin everything we do. Edward Wilson didn’t achieve anything alone; he knew the importance of teamwork and so do we. Our school values ensure that everyone in the team feels safe and welcome. As a UNICEF Rights Respecting School, our pupils care for our immediate and global community and demonstrate this through their kindness, celebration of diversity and hard work.
Our school values communicate what we all stand for:
RESPECT: We care for each other and take account of other people's feelings and rights. We respect property.
COMMUNITY: We are a school community and we work together. We make links with our local area and beyond.
PERSEVERANCE: We keep trying. We love challenge and push ourselves to the limit of our potential.
KINDNESS: We are friendly, considerate and supportive. We include everyone in our learning and games.
HONESTY: We tell the truth. We do the right thing, even if no one is watching.
CURIOSITY: We are excited to learn and find out more about the world and each other. We demonstrate hard work.
Our mascot, Teddy Wilson, exemplifies these values, which are woven into school life through assemblies, rewards, our exciting enrichment offer and all our interactions.
Our curriculum is challenging, broad and relevant to our community. Teachers take a creative approach when planning sequences of learning, and our pupils are given opportunities to experiment, investigate and develop research skills. We are proud of our pupil achievement and our Outstanding provision for Personal Development. With our autism and Visual Impairment provision, we are establishing ourselves as a centre of excellence for SEND and know this means better learning for all pupils: a rising tide lifts all boats.
Our pupils are happy and enjoy school. If you are a prospective parent, then I look forward to showing you our school: please contact the office to arrange a visit!
Katy Lawrence Headteacher

Breakfast and After School Club
We offer a full wrap-around provision from 8.00 am to 5.45 pm. This is open to all pupils.
Edward Wilson Primary School's Breakfast Club aims to provide pupils with a safe and fun place to start their school day. Breakfast wraparound begins at 8am and is open to all pupils from Reception to Year 6 and is run by our own staff members.
We provide a space for reading and quiet activities, as well as more structured activities such as board games. A nutritious breakfast is provided each morning, and the children will be encouraged to enjoy their breakfast while talking together with their friends and our staff. At the end of the session, we hope that the children will be fed, happy and ready to learn.
The provision runs from 8:00am – 8:45am every weekday during term time (excluding Inset days). At the end of the sessions, the children will be escorted to their class for the start of the regular school day.

The cost of the club is £2 per day, per child (with additional siblings then costing 50p each).
Please book a place with the office.
Our After School Club runs from 3.15pm (the end of the regular school day) until 5.45pm, for pupils in Reception to Year 6 and costs £8 per session.

Children are welcome to attend regularly and on an ad-hoc, occasional basis.
Full wraparound childcare (8am – 5.45pm) plus snacks, is offered for a very affordable £10 per day!

Minutes from the Full Governing Board meetings can be found below, as can details of our Governing Board, including the names, areas of responsibility and terms of appointment for each governor. Governors are kept informed about the progress and key information about the school through:
Working with the Headteacher, the SLT and other Leads, the Governors play an important role in helping shape and develop the strategic direction of the school; providing skilled support and challenge to ensure that our aspirational targets are achieved.
Simon has been a governor at Edward Wilson Primary School since 2016 and serves as Chair of the Governing Body.
Professionally, Simon works in cyber security, technology and risk management, bringing senior leadership experience from government, financial and professional services. He also represents primary school governors on Westminster’s Schools Forum, contributing to wider discussions on education and school funding across the borough.
As Chair, Simon works closely with the Headteacher and Governing Body to provide strategic leadership, support and constructive challenge. He is committed to ensuring Edward Wilson remains an inclusive, ambitious and supportive school where every child has the opportunity to thrive.

Previously she worked for Amazon for almost 7 years in Seattle and London, with roles across e-commerce, Alexa, and corporate strategy. As the first in her family to attend university, Felicia is deeply passionate about social mobility, childhood literacy, and diversity, equity, and inclusion. As an avid reader, she volunteered with Reading to Kids when living in Los Angeles California, and is currently also the Executive Sponsor for BT in Women@Tech, a consortium of 10 large technology firms, driving gender parity in the workplace.

She has two children who attend the school and is passionate about supporting the school community and helping children to thrive. Outside of school, Fahimah enjoys reading, baking and hiking.

Thomas is currently an Associate at Herbert Smith Freehills, a leading international law firm, where he specialises in commercial litigation and dispute resolution. Thomas has previous experience of working with children and was formerly employed as a drama teacher at the European School in Brussels, Belgium.

pageCache.pageTitle: Edward Wilson Primary School - Remote Learning
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
This information is intended to provide clarity to pupils and parents or carers about what to expect from remote education where national or local restrictions require entire cohorts to remain at home. Guidance from the Department for Education advises that remote learning should only be used as a last resort when in-person attendance is impossible.
A pupil’s first day or two of being educated remotely might look different from our standard approach, while we take all necessary actions to prepare for a longer period of remote teaching.
What should my child expect from immediate remote education in the first day or two of pupils being sent home?
Teachers will set work and tasks via Google Classroom (GC) for all pupils to complete. Weekly homework tasks are set on GC throughout the year so all pupils have an understanding of how to access this. Additionally, the school will aim to provide devices to families, on a case-by-case basis. If this is the case for you, please discuss this with a member of the office team.
The school will send an email to all families on the day following the pupils being sent home to remind parents and pupils of how to access work and support.
Following the first few days of remote education, will my child be taught broadly the same curriculum as they would if they were in school?
We teach the same curriculum remotely as we do in school and will follow the timetable for each class which they would usually follow in school.
For some curriculum resources, which rely on equipment/software/resources we have in school (which it would be unlikely that most families have at home, e.g. Computing, PE and Music), teachers will adapt lessons and longer-term plans to ensure topics covered can be accessed by our pupils remotely.
Teacher support can be accessed via messaging on GC (where teachers will be online each morning), or via a weekly phone call the class teacher will make to each family.
Assemblies and story times will be available regularly via GC and the school website.
How long can I expect work set by the school to take my child each day?
We expect that remote education (including remote teaching and independent work) will take pupils broadly 3-4 hours each day. In line with the SEND Code of Practice, we will adjust this expectation if necessary for a child with additional needs.
Each pupil has a GC login which they can use to access teacher support, complete work and submit tasks for feedback. Pupils are well-practised at using GC as weekly homework is set on this platform.
If necessary, timetables, guidance for logging in to GC and help sheets for online learning will be available on the school website to support remote education.
Through weekly phone calls between the class teacher and families, support can be given if there are any access issues.
How will my child be taught remotely?
We use a combination of the following approaches to teach pupils remotely:
What are your expectations for my child’s engagement and the support that we as parents and carers should provide at home?
We expect pupils to complete remote learning for each day they would usually attend school e.g. term-time, Monday to Friday.
In Years 3-6, the majority of pupils should be able to complete the work set independently, with only the need for adult supervision during live video calls (morning meetings) and support as they require.
Younger pupils, in the EYFS or Key Stage 1, or pupils with additional needs, will require additional support, particularly with logging in, opening tasks and submitting assignments. However, even our youngest pupils should be able to complete tasks independently.
In all year groups, the class teacher will be available each morning between 9am to 12pm on GC to provide feedback on any uploaded learning.
How will you check whether my child is engaging with their work and how will I be informed if there are concerns?
Pupils are expected to turn in/submit assignments on a daily basis and join morning meetings as often as they are able to.
If a class teacher has concerns that no, or too little work, is being submitted or completed, they will initially make contact on GC via a message. In the event that this does not lead to work being completed, the class teacher will call the family to discuss this with either the parent or carer.
If a pupil continues not to engage with remote learning across a longer period, a member of the school’s leadership team will arrange a meeting over the phone with the family to support their child in engaging with remote lessons.
Feedback can take many forms and may not always mean extensive written comments for individual children. For example, whole-class feedback or quizzes marked automatically via digital platforms are also valid and effective methods, amongst many others. Our approach to feeding back on pupil work is as follows:
Teachers will be online each morning for a minimum of three hours during which time they are responding to pupils’ queries, providing feedback and providing additional support as required. Any work submitted in the afternoon or evening would be looked at the following morning.
All pupils will receive personalised written feedback at least once per day on GC which may consist of a positive comment, highlighting of a misconception along with support in addressing this, suggestions for how work could be further improved or an additional challenge.
During weekly phone calls home, teachers will provide personalised verbal feedback to the pupil which will also be shared with their parent or carer. Teachers will also provide generalised feedback to the whole class during the daily morning meetings, including the addressing of common misconceptions or suggestions for how most pupils can improve the quality of their work.
Where additional tasks are set on commercial websites, marking and feedback will be provided automatically by the website. This will be looked over by the class teacher on a regular basis and may be referenced during weekly phone calls.
How will you work with me to help my child who needs additional support from adults at home to access remote education?
We recognise that some pupils, for example some pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), may not be able to access remote education without support from adults at home. We acknowledge the difficulties this may place on families, and we will work with parents and carers to support those pupils in the following ways:
Unless advised otherwise by Westminster/the DfE, all pupils with Education, Health and Care Plans will be able to continue to attend school full-time throughout the closure period. This means that they have access to all the remote learning as well as the opportunity to work with staff in school using a range of resources and equipment. We will provide extra support for pupils with additional needs if they choose not to attend school, including regular phone calls from the SENDCo to ensure that they are managing online learning. We will also provide extra physical resource packs for those pupils that are finding it difficult to access online learning.
Specialist teachers, including our QTVI and SENDCo, will continue to provide both support in school and online as appropriate. The SENDCo will continue to liaise with other professionals to offer support and advice for learning during this time, including working with Educational Psychologists, Speech and Language Therapists and Occupational Therapists.
Teachers will provide a range of resources for online learning to engage younger pupils as well as those with additional needs, including morning meetings in person, videos and presentations. We will also provide learning resource packs for pupils in EYFS.
If my child is not in school because they are self-isolating, how will their remote education differ from the approaches described above?
In the event of a pupil self-isolating, where they are well enough to learn, the class teacher will upload the lesson materials they are using within the classroom on to GC for self-isolating pupils to remotely access. In addition to the Designated Safeguarding Leader, our Attendance Officer will also be in regular contact with the family to provide any necessary support.

Building Works and SEND Expansion
SEND Expansion
From September 2026, Seals class is opening on the first floor. We are excited about the further developments that will be happening to make our school site even more SEND-friendly (and engaging for all pupils) during this academic year:
A 'Body Shop' room opposite Seals on the first floor. This will be accessible to all pupils at the school and will develop gross motor skills, hand-eye coordination, turn-taking, teamwork, balance, agility and many other skills
A Calming Room adjoining the Seals classroom. This will be a quiet, safe place to take part in small-scale games and to co- or self-regulate when a child is upset
Arctic Terns: a darkened, relaxing room on the second floor with the option for music and LED lights but also for calming moments with minimal sensory stimulation
Roof Works
Also in 2026-27, our wonderful roof playground is receiving a makeover! Although most of the water ingress has been fixed, we need to make sure our historic and beautiful site is future-proofed, so building contractors will be on site in September, and again at the start of 2027, to take up the existing surface and investigate the leaks. Following this, the playground will be reinstated and will be better than ever.
Painting and Decorating
We are delighted to work with the Paddington Partnership, a local corporate volunteer organisation, who came in over the summer holidays and painted the top and middle halls and a number of classrooms. There were over 100 volunteers on site and their fantastic work can be seen on a video here:

Special Resource Provision (SRP) for Pupils with Autism
Welcome to Learning Explorers: Our Special Resource Provision (SRP) for Pupils with Autism
At Edward Wilson Primary School, we are proud to provide a specialist education within our mainstream school. Known as Learning Explorers, our provision consists of three dedicated classes—Penguins, Polar Bears and Seals—each with a capacity for six pupils.
Our Team
Pupils in Learning Explorers are supported by a highly experienced and passionate teaching team. This includes a Lead Teacher (SENDCo), a Class Teacher, and a group of skilled Teaching Assistants. Together, they create a nurturing and engaging environment where every child can thrive. The expertise within the SRP team reflects our Number 1 School Development Priority: to establish Edward Wilson as a centre of excellence for SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities).
Our Approach
We have designed a bespoke curriculum tailored to the unique needs of each pupil in the provision. Lessons are carefully planned and adapted to align with individual targets, ensuring personalised learning opportunities.
Whenever possible, pupils are supported to learn alongside peers in mainstream classrooms and engage in mainstream activities e.g. playtime, trips and assemblies. This inclusive approach reflects our belief that every child can achieve their potential with the right support and opportunities.
Support for Families and Collaboration with Professionals
We understand that families of children with SEND often face unique challenges. Our team is committed to working closely with parents and carers, providing ongoing support and guidance. We also collaborate with a range of professionals, including:
Additionally, we can signpost families to external support organisations to ensure they have access to a wide network of resources.
Westminster’s SEND and Autism Outreach teams
Speech and Language Therapists
Educational Psychologists
Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists
Admissions
Admission to Learning Explorers is managed through consultations with Westminster Local Authority. Applications are reviewed by the Headteacher, SENDCo, and SEND Link Governor against our entry criteria, which you can view here.

Provision for Pupils with a Vision Impairment
Welcome to our Provision for Pupils with a Vision Impairment (VI)
At Edward Wilson Primary School, we are proud to host a specialist provision for pupils with a vision impairment (VI), established over twenty years ago, in September 2005. Our goal is to provide full inclusion for visually impaired children within a mainstream primary school setting. Over the years, we have supported numerous pupils in developing the educational and life skills needed for a smooth transition to Key Stage 3 and beyond.
In addition to supporting pupils at Edward Wilson, we offer outreach services to children and young adults with vision impairments across Westminster, reinforcing our commitment to inclusion and accessibility.
Our Team and Approach Our VI provision is led by a Qualified Teacher of Visually Impaired children (QTVI), who specialises in creating and delivering tailored support for pupils with sight loss. The QTVI works collaboratively with mainstream teachers to adapt class teaching and learning and ensure interventions are impactful and reviewed regularly, ensuring that every pupil can access the curriculum and make progress from her/his starting points.
Key aspects of our provision include:
Support Beyond the Classroom We recognise that pupils with a visual impairment and their families may face unique challenges throughout their educational journey. Our QTVI, along with other professionals, provides emotional and practical support during key moments such as transitions or changes in a pupil’s vision.
We have strong partnerships with trusted organisations like the RNIB, Guide Dogs, and Westminster's Sensory Support Outreach Team. Additionally, we liaise closely with parents and caregivers to ensure that self-help strategies are consistently applied at home and school.
What We Offer As a dedicated Alternative Resource Provision for pupils with a visual impairment, we are committed to providing:
A Community of Inclusion and Achievement At Edward Wilson Primary School, we have high expectations for all our pupils and firmly believe that every child has the ability to succeed. Our provision for visually impaired pupils ensures they receive the specialised support they need to thrive while enjoying the benefits of an inclusive education.
Find out more about the VI Resource Base at Edward Wilson by clicking the link below (You will find a video in the 'Whole School' section called 'The VI Unit').
